en: able to understand situations quickly and gain an advantage
ex: An astute investor, she sold her shares before the crash.
The perceptive teacher noticed that the student was upset.

en: having good judgment, especially in taste
ex: Discerning readers will notice the hidden clues in chapter two.
Her incisive questions exposed the weaknesses of the plan.
Credulous readers shared the fake story thousands of times.

en: showing a lack of experience or judgment
ex: It was naive to think the project would be finished in a week.
The rebels held clandestine meetings at night.
The agency ran a covert operation to rescue the hostages.

en: done secretly because it would not be approved
ex: He took a surreptitious look at his phone during the exam.
The bright red car was conspicuous in the parking lot.
The essay was a blatant copy of an online article.
There was no overt hostility, but the tension was clear.

en: so intense it seems almost touchable
ex: The excitement in the stadium was palpable.

en: very clear and obvious, often unpleasantly
ex: The photos show a stark contrast between the two neighborhoods.
A good dictionary is indispensable for language learners.

en: necessary to make a whole complete
ex: Music is an integral part of the school's culture.
The meeting was a pivotal moment in the company's history.
Safety is paramount in any science lab.
They argued over a trivial detail for an hour.

uz: hisobga olmasa ham bo'ladigan darajada kichik
en: so small it can be ignored
ex: The difference in price is negligible.

en: of secondary importance; on the edge
ex: The film's peripheral characters get little screen time.

en: existing only on the surface; not thorough
ex: The article offers only a superficial analysis of the problem.
The rug has an intricate pattern of flowers and birds.

en: extremely complex and difficult to follow
ex: The convoluted instructions confused everyone.
The book offers a nuanced view of the war.
Climate change is a multifaceted problem.
He has only a rudimentary knowledge of French.

en: severe or plain in style; without comfort
ex: The monks lived in austere rooms with only a bed and a desk.
The book brings together disparate ideas from art and science.

en: made up of different kinds of things
ex: The class is heterogeneous, with students of many ages and backgrounds.
She has an eclectic taste in music, from jazz to folk.
The heart is analogous to a pump.

en: of the same kind throughout; uniform
ex: The town's population was once fairly homogeneous.
Some archaic laws are still on the books but never enforced.
Floppy disks are now obsolete.
The school uses innovative methods to teach science.

en: introducing new ideas or methods for the first time
ex: Her groundbreaking research changed how doctors treat burns.

en: generous or forgiving, especially toward a rival
ex: The champion was magnanimous in victory and praised her opponent.
A benevolent donor paid for the new library.
Her altruistic work in the clinic earned her national praise.
The avaricious landlord raised the rent every year.
Critics called the sequel a mercenary attempt to cash in on the first film.
In a candid interview, the actor discussed his failures.
She was forthright about the risks of the surgery.

en: not sincere; pretending to know less than one does
ex: It was disingenuous of him to claim he had never seen the email.
The duplicitous agent worked for both governments.
The ad made the specious claim that the pill could cure any illness.
The study found a spurious link between shoe size and intelligence.

en: wanting to avoid activity or work
ex: The indolent cat slept in the sun all afternoon.
The heat made everyone feel lethargic.
Many young people are apathetic about local politics.
He tried to look nonchalant, but his hands were shaking.
The new manager seemed aloof at first but was actually shy.

en: having great energy for a cause
ex: The zealous fans waited outside the stadium all night.
She is a fervent supporter of animal rights.

en: having a keen interest in something
ex: He is an avid reader of science fiction.
Too much screen time can be detrimental to sleep.

en: causing harm, often in a way that is not obvious
ex: The chemical has deleterious effects on fish.

en: having a harmful effect in a gradual or subtle way
ex: Rumors can have a pernicious effect on a team's morale.
The flight was delayed because of adverse weather.

en: producing good effects, often after something unpleasant
ex: Failing the first test was a salutary lesson.
A quiet room is conducive to concentration.

en: giving a good chance of success
ex: It was a propitious moment to launch the new product.
Judges must remain impartial.
Scientists try to be objective when reporting results.

en: not influenced by strong emotion; rational
ex: The report gives a dispassionate account of the riot.

en: strongly supporting one party or cause
ex: Partisan arguments made compromise impossible.

en: promoting a particular point of view
ex: The tendentious article ignored all evidence against the author's view.

en: existing as a natural, permanent quality
ex: There are risks inherent in any sport.
The painting has little intrinsic value but great sentimental value.

en: existing but not yet developed or visible
ex: The coach saw latent talent in the quiet young player.
The volcano has been dormant for centuries.
There was an implicit agreement that no one would mention the accident.
The teacher gave explicit instructions for the project.
The peace agreement remains fragile.
